title: Algebraic Combinations and Natural Domains
originalTopic: Combining Functions: Sums, Differences, and Products
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Let f(x) = x and g(x) = sqrt(x - 1). Determine formulas for (f + g)(x) and (f * g)(x), and specify their natural domains.

steps.title: Find the Individual Domains
steps.explanation: The linear polynomial f(x) = x is defined for all real numbers. For g(x) = sqrt(x - 1), the square root requires the radicand to be non-negative: x - 1 >= 0, which yields x >= 1.
steps.why: The natural domain of an even radical requires non-negative radicands.

steps.title: Intersect Individual Domains
steps.explanation: By the definition of algebraic combinations, the sum and product functions are defined on the intersection of their individual domains.
steps.why: Both component functions must be simultaneously well-defined on the real line.

steps.title: Write the Combined Formulas
steps.explanation: Add and multiply the expressions directly according to functional arithmetic.
steps.why: Standard definition of pointwise addition and multiplication of functions.
